summary: Used Ansible (run from node2, the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed, acting as control node) to blacklist the usb-storage kernel module on node1. The playbook creates /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with `blacklist usb-storage` and `install usb-storage /bin/false`, runs update-initramfs -u, and ensures the module isn't currently loaded via community.general.modprobe. Had to first bootstrap sshd on node1 (missing host keys) and set up key-based root SSH from node2, since the default ansible.cfg assumed a pre-provisioned 'antrieb' user that doesn't exist on this vanilla Ubuntu image. Verified modprobe usb-storage fails (rc=1) and the module stays unloaded, both before and after restarting node1. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured boot_id baselines, restarted each node one at a time, confirmed boot_id changed after each restart, and verified recovery (blacklist enforced on node1; ansible control tooling and connectivity to node1 recovered on node2, confirmed via an idempotent playbook re-run showing changed=0).
actions_performed: Checked node1 and node2 for ansible availability; node2 has ansible-core 2.20.5 + community.general 12.6.0, so it served as the Ansible control node
Captured pre-change baseline on node1: usb-storage not loaded (lsmod empty), no blacklist file present
Diagnosed and fixed non-functional sshd on node1 (missing host keys) via ssh-keygen -A and systemctl restart ssh
Set up passwordless root SSH from node2 to node1 using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY

Wrote Ansible inventory (/root/ansible/inventory.ini) and playbook (/root/ansible/blacklist-usb-storage.yml) on node2, overriding the default ansible.cfg (which assumed a non-existent 'antrieb' user) to connect as root using the cluster SSH key
Ran the playbook: created /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf (blacklist + install /bin/false), ran update-initramfs -u, ensured usb-storage absent
Verified immediate effect: modprobe usb-storage now fails with rc=1 and lsmod stays empty
Captured boot_id baselines for node1 and node2 before restarting either
Restarted node1 via backgrounded `reboot`, polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified on node1 post-reboot: blacklist file intact, module still blocked by modprobe, lsmod empty
Restarted node2 via backgrounded `reboot`, polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified node2 recovery: ansible tooling functional, re-ran playbook against node1 showing changed=0 (idempotent), confirming persisted state and restored cross-node connectivity

evidence.requirement: usb-storage module blacklisted on node1 (immediate + persistent)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no blacklist file and module unloaded; after the Ansible playbook ran (changed=2), /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf was created, initramfs updated, and modprobe usb-storage explicitly failed (rc=1) confirming the block is active immediately.

evidence.summary: Confirmed node2 has ansible/ansible-playbook (node1 does not) and used node2 as the control node to run the blacklist playbook against node1 over SSH.
